Otto Grit.listen: the drunk pull: snare rushes early, kick leans back late, hats dead straight; half SP-1200 dust; vinyl bed; keys, guitar and horn chops; his stamp is a dusty tom on the tail of bars 4 and 8
Otto Grit._research_note: REBUILT 2026-10-24 (Original side). Era per owner 2026-09-06: the general dusty Dilla 1992-2003 (J Dillo keeps Donuts). Transcript: Handoffs/DJ Rebuild/Otto Grit/research transcript.md. PHRASE-TO-SETTING MAP. 'snare rushes early, kick leans back late, hats dead straight' = lanes offsets (CONFIRMED by Hein, Soundfly, Big Noise, Charnas; the ms values are the engine's, NOT FOUND in sources). 'half SP-1200 dust; vinyl bed' = dust .25 / vinyl -48 (SP-1200 early CONFIRMED by Dilla himself and R.J. Rice; vinyl bed carried over, unsourced). 'keys, guitar and horn chops' = signature.chord_source: midi 75 / loop 10 / packs 15, with piano 3.75, guitar 2.25, horns 1.5 as the researched half (order sourced: Rhodes/piano, samba guitar on Runnin', Mangione horn on Fall in Love [UNSURE]; magnitudes are mine) and the other 8 sounds sharing 7.5. 'dusty tom on bars 4 and 8' = stamp lane, kept as the identity's own signature (NOT FOUND in research). tempo [79, 95] from Runnin' 94, Drop 95, Fall in Love 91-94, She Said 79 (BPMs from Tunebat/SongBPM). Roots Bb x3 (Runnin', Drop, Fall in Love remix are A#m), F#, Eb (Badu Eb dorian); dorian added. Magnitudes mine.

Cutz.listen: New York 1992-96 jazz-sample boom bap, 83 to 98 bpm: 53% swing, a little behind the beat; hard kick and snare cut from old breaks, with ghost snares; piano and guitar loops chopped small with gaps; stamp is a scratched vocal hook closing bars 4 and 8 (placement carried over)

Crate Prophet.listen: New York 1991-94 sample-chop boom-bap, 87 to 102 bpm: warm and loose with 60% golden-era swing (carried over, not sourced); crunchy 12-bit drums under the heaviest vinyl bed plus record wow; hats on eighths; horns and piano chops over a walking bass line; snare sits LATE (era-driven, flagged, carried over: house verdict is early, but laid-back is this character); loose congas, stamp is a conga slap on bars 4/8 (carried over). This is also the prototype that SKIPS sidechain (the 1-in-10 no-duck rule)

Chrome Dial.listen: Virginia 1996-2002 bounce: stuttering, sparse syncopation with silence as an instrument — bar 6 drops to almost nothing and answers bar 5; kick lands in odd spots, claps and snares answer; tabla, shaker and conga off-center as the rhythm; a plucked or flute-like lead over a rubbery bass, in minor or phrygian_dominant; clean (the grit is arrangement, not crush); stamp is an exotic perc hit late in bars 4/8

Glass Cat.listen: minimal and dry, with thin synth keys and a plucked, clavichord-style line: NO hats — a snap keeps time; the clap lands ~18 ms LATE against the snare (the documented Neptunes flam); bar 8 stop-starts. The Alt file is the one to compare hard: era says bone dry, house says gated. Stamp is a weird click/zap on bars 4/8

Rage Engine._no_twist: Owner's personal-twist rule (2026-09-03) is vetoed here BY HIS OWN CALL: his research says the mix is glued by saturation, not modulation, and a wall of sound has no gap for a delay. He still gets the house mix EQ. Do not add echo/chorus/phaser without asking him.

New Math.listen: the new one. A club kick pattern that never sits where trap taught you to expect it; a hat lane counting FIVE against everyone else's four (quintuplet grid); percussion running world-rhythm math (E(7,16) and E(5,16) necklaces); and one lane swinging 58% while the rest of the kit stays dead straight — the clash IS the groove. Clean and punchy, mid-forward kick. Stamp is a found-sound fx hit on the tail of bars 4/8

Half Light.listen: the slowest thing in the room. Half the roster's tempo, and every lane drags BEHIND the click on purpose (kick +26 ms, snare +34 ms) — nobody else is late by design. No hats at all: a cross-stick rim keeps time in threes over a four grid, so it never lines up twice the same way. The backbeat mostly refuses to show — the snare sits on the 4 alone and leaves the 2 empty. Tape wow is the highest on the roster, so the whole thing sags and recovers. Gated snare like the house, but his Alt file is a HALL — 2.2 seconds, the biggest room any DJ has. Stamp is a reversed hit at the END of bars 2 and 6, so it sucks INTO bars 3 and 7 — everyone else stamps the tail of 4 and 8; he arrives early instead.

Fast Water.listen: the fastest thing in the room and it doesn't sound fast. The kick and snare play HALFTIME — two moves a bar, so the pulse feels like 86 — while the break lane runs 32nds on top at the full 172. That lane is the loudest non-backbone lane on the roster (0.52 against everyone else's 0.26-0.4): the chop is the beat, not the garnish. Snare never sits on the 2 and 4 — it lands on the 2 and the '&' of 3, the jungle two-step. Ghost snares sit UNDER it at a whisper. Everything is nudged EARLY, not late (break -7 ms, ghosts -11 ms) — he pulls where Half Light drags. Straight 50% swing everywhere: at this tempo swing turns to mud. Gated snare like the house, Alt is a short PLATE (0.9 s) — bright and small, so the break stays readable. Stamp is a siren/reverse hit on the DOWNBEAT of bars 5 and 8 — he announces the bar instead of tailing it.
